assertion_audit:
Assertions reviewed at 2f9c68d4097748ea184b7d6f1e7d0cf00cb254d3:
Line 19: decoded payload equals the file fixture; fails if reader returns None, malformed or altered data.
Line 20: first decode count equals one; fails if first call performs no decode or extra decodes, giving the counter a positive control.
Line 21: repeated payload equals fixture; fails if the cache returns a different record.
Line 22: second decode count remains one; restoring the original uncached reader makes it two, as negative-control.log actually records.
Line 31: original payload is pending; fails if the reader does not load the original file.
Line 32: original read counts one decode; fails for missing or duplicate initial decode.
Line 34: inode is unchanged; fails if the test fixture replaces rather than rewrites the file.
Line 35: returned payload has the rewritten answer; removing invalidation makes it pending and fails this assertion.
Line 36: total decode count equals two; disabling invalidation gives one and redundant parsing gives more than two.
Line 49 (both parameter values): after changing nested answer to acted and adding an extra field, the next read equals the separately retained pending fixture; omitting copy isolation outside regions shares the cached nested list, and omitting mutable=True inside a region refuses the mutation before this assertion. A shared mutable cache inside the region also fails the pending comparison.
No assertion compares the result to a value mutated alongside it: json.dumps(expected) writes bytes, the reader parses distinct objects, and expected remains unchanged during the deliberate returned-object mutation.
